transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-11
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramirez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connor (OxfordTek Head of Security), Nora Chen (Platform Lead), Rajiv Malhotra (DevOps), Maya Singh (Compliance)
Shared links: security_matrix_v1.xlsx (drive), pilot-results-20261111.csv (drive), oxfordtek-saml-metadata.xml (pending)

Summary:
Quick sync on pilot security posture; main items SSO setup, audit log format/retention, SOC2 evidence backlog, and a small performance note on caching and log volume. Agreed on targeted next steps and dates.

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um we'll do a quick round, aim for 45-ish minutes and then any open questions last 10.
[00:12] Liam: hey thanks, yeah we have Maya and Rajiv on the line as well. Quick ask — want to make sure the logs capture username/email for audit trails, retention controls are enforced, and that we can show this for our SOC 2 readiness.
[00:26] Nora: also curious about SSO flow - last time we saw the dev preview the redirect flow didn't preserve the tenant claim.
[00:38] Diego: noted, thanks. We made a change last week to include tenant_id in the auth payload but that was OIDC-first; for your stack you said SAML so we'll confirm mapping for NameID + attributes.
[00:52] Rajiv: for SSO we prefer SAML 2.0 and unique persistent NameID, we don't want transient.
[01:05] Samira: got it, we'll treat SAML as first-class for the POC. Liam, can you send the metadata?
[01:12] Liam: working on it. I can provision a test IdP tomorrow and push the metadata link.
[01:20] Maya: retention — we need logs retained 2 years for security telemetry but PII scrubbed to 6 months unless flagged. Can you support selective retention?
[01:35] Priya: yes we support policy tags on events, the retention engine can apply differential windows per tag, we just need your mapping.
[01:44] Diego: technical note — audit logs are emitted as JSON lines with a header that includes request_id, model_variant, tenant_id, user_id (if available), and token counts. Right now retention is time-based only but we can scope tag-based TTL.
[02:00] Nora: sample schema?
[02:04] Diego: I'll paste an example in Confluence after this call, but sample fields: timestamp, request_id, user_id_or_null, tenant_id, model, prompt_hash, latency_ms, token_in, token_out, decision_flags.
[02:22] Liam: good. For SOC2 we'll need proof that logs are immutable and that we can export them for audits. Are logs stored in a customer-controlled bucket?
[02:35] Samira: currently pilot uses Redwood-hosted encrypted buckets; for Private customers we offer options to push logs to your S3/gcs or VPC flow — for the POC we can push a copy to your S3 and also retain an encrypted canonical copy.
[02:51] Maya: what's the encryption at rest policy? KMS? HSM?
[02:56] Diego: AES-256 with customer-managed KMS on Private; hosted uses Redwood KMS but key separation per tenant. We also support HSM-backed keys for enterprise.
[03:08] Rajiv: latency impact? encrypt/decrypt per request could add overhead.
[03:13] Diego: negligible for log writes; for inference artifact we only decrypt model cache metadata not the model weights on request path — so minimal latency change. We saw a 3-4% p99 increase in a tiny internal test but that's with synchronous external KMS calls; with local KMS agent it's sub-1%.
[03:32] Samira: quick pilot results slide — Diego, can you walk through numbers?
[03:37] Diego: sure, pulled sample from last 48 hours, baseline run 1: average latency 78ms for prompt size ~120 tokens, kv caching on gave us token cost reduction ~28% and 10-15ms improvement on median latency. Under 10k RPS spike the fallback to a compatible quantized model increased latency to ~210ms but success rate maintained.
[04:05] Nora: that's helpful; for our SLA we want p95 < 300ms which looks okay. Cost numbers?
[04:12] Diego: token cost per 1k tokens about $0.95 on hosted baseline, with caching and quant we saw effective unit down to $0.68 in the sample workload. We'll share the spreadsheet.
[04:25] Liam: back to security — audit log retention and export for auditors is key. We need an export job that can deliver a zipped set with manifest and a signed hash.
[04:38] Priya: we have an export utility, we can sign manifests with Redwood KMS or with your customer-managed key — and provide an SHA256 summary file per archive.
[04:49] Maya: okay we prefer customer-managed signing.
[04:52] Diego: we'll validate that with a spike.
[04:55] Samira: SOC2 evidence — we know this is on your timeline, Liam. What artifacts do you need from us?
[05:03] Liam: primarily access control lists, SSO configuration screenshots, retention policy docs, sample audit logs, and a diagram of where keys live. Also request chain for incident response.
[05:15] Samira: understood, I'll compile the initial package; Priya will walk the evidence during the SOC2 demo.
[05:22] Nora: timeline — internal auditor wants to see preliminary artifacts by end of month.
[05:28] Maya: earlier if possible.
[05:31] Samira: we'll aim for EOM; action item for Samira to upload a security matrix with links to artifacts by 11/18.
[05:40] Rajiv: about the SSO metadata — when we tested earlier, the SAML assertion didn't include group claims. We rely on group mapping to set roles. Can Redwood accept groups mapped in the AttributeStatement?
[05:52] Diego: yes, we map groups from AttributeStatement to RBAC roles. There is a default mapping but you can override via the Console or the API.
[06:02] Rajiv: good. Also need to know how long audit logs are kept in the host bucket before transfer to cold storage.
[06:10] Diego: by default logs are hot for 90 days, then move to cold for 15 months — that's the hosted default. For your requirement of 24 months we can extend cold retention or export to your long-term storage.
[06:25] Maya: we will want different retention for PII vs non-PII, so we need tagging at ingestion.
[06:31] Diego: ingestion tagging supported — we'll need an attribute on the event to mark pii:true/false, Diego to share sample ingestion snippet.
[06:39] Samira: ok next, about the pilot's access model — who in OxfordTek will have admin vs viewer roles in the Console during POC?
[06:48] Nora: Liam and Rajiv admin, Maya compliance viewer, devs get viewer+deploy.
[06:55] Samira: we'll provision those roles once SSO is live, otherwise we can create invites via email.
[07:01] Liam: prefer SSO so it's auditable.
[07:04] Diego: noted. On the audit logs, one more nuance: we currently include prompt hashes not raw prompts in the default logs for privacy. If you need raw prompts for debugging, that is opt-in and flagged as PII.
[07:18] Rajiv: we may need raw prompts for a short window for evaluation, can you do ephemeral storage?
[07:24] Diego: yes ephemeral debug logs retained for 7 days and then deleted; we can keep a snapshot on your S3 if you want longer.
[07:33] Maya: confirm deletion policy meets legal hold exceptions?
[07:37] Priya: we can pause deletion for specific audit requests; that's manual process and requires an owner and timestamp.
[07:46] Samira: let's cover SOC2 walk-through next week, 30 minutes, Priya will run it.
[07:51] Priya: will send invite for 11/19.
[07:55] Nora: quick procurement question — any blockers for us to move from hosted pilot to dedicated reserved capacity? Will it require data migration?
[08:05] Diego: migration is mostly config and flipping an endpoint; data like logs can be migrated via export jobs; models are available across both. We have a migration guide we'll share.
[08:17] Samira: I'll attach migration guide in the follow-up.
[08:21] Liam: do you have pen-test reports?
[08:24] Samira: yes, we have a recent pentest summary and remediation list, will include in the security matrix.
[08:31] Diego: small note on cost/latency tradeoff: if you lock dedicated capacity you get lower p99 and more consistent latency but billing is committed; in pilot hosted is more elastic but can have tail spikes.
[08:46] Nora: understood.
[08:48] Maya: any compliance certifications beyond SOC2?
[08:52] Samira: currently SOC2 Type II in progress, ISO 27001 planned for next quarter, and we support HIPAA controls for healthcare workloads.
[09:02] Liam: good. On action items again, we need a sample signed export by next Tuesday to show auditors.
[09:10] Diego: Diego will run a signed export spike and attach a sample.
[09:16] Rajiv: what about retention of embeddings and caches — are they considered logs?
[09:22] Diego: embeddings are separate artifact and have their own retention policy; by default we treat them as derived non-PII but if you store user-specific embeddings we can tag them as PII.
[09:33] Nora: ok. Are there rate limits on audit export?
[09:37] Diego: exports can be throttled; we'll provide a bulk export API for audits to avoid rate limit problems.
[09:44] Liam: perfect.
[09:46] Samira: recap — Samira will upload security matrix and pentest summary, Diego to run audit-log spike and signed export, Priya to schedule SOC2 demo 11/19, Liam to upload SAML metadata 11/17, Maya to send retention buckets and PII rules 11/16.
[10:10] Nora: sounds good.
[10:12] Samira: any other concerns?
[10:15] Maya: just ensure we have an auditable chain for who requested PII hold.
[10:21] Priya: will put a playbook together and share in Confluence.
[10:27] Samira: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the notes and share the artifacts shortly.
[10:33] Liam: thanks all.
[10:35] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcription had trouble with some proper names (OxfordTek stakeholders) and with a few technical acronyms; speaker labels occasionally merged.
notes: Spike to produce signed export (sample) requested; SAML metadata pending from customer; security matrix and pentest summary to be uploaded by Redwood.
